label: September 1917
headline: The Harvest Moon Raids
deck: Night bombers strike London; Russia is proclaimed a republic
caption: Londoners crowd an Underground platform at night, sheltering from bombs
body: With the nights bright under the harvest moon, German Gotha bombers come over London again and again at the end of September, six raids in eight nights. The damage is not great, but thousands of Londoners now spend their nights in the Underground stations.

In Russia General Kornilov, the commander-in-chief, sends troops towards Petrograd early in the month. Kerensky calls him a traitor, railwaymen stop the trains, and the soldiers are talked out of their march. On 14 September Russia is proclaimed a republic, and the Bolsheviks, armed against Kornilov, keep their arms.
On the Euphrates, British and Indian troops surround the town of Ramadi and take it on 28 September with some 3,500 prisoners.
briefs: A Fatherland Party is founded in Germany against a compromise peace
The Bolsheviks win a majority in the Petrograd Soviet
Argentina is angered by German cables sent through Sweden
